name: Shrimp Pink
lede: Shrimp Pink is a light yellowish pink from Ridgway's 1912 plates, called sakura-iro — cherry blossom color — in Japan, and the English phrase peaked in print in 1929.

sections.title: Cherry blossom color
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 plates give Shrimp Pink at hue 5, tone f, on plate I, and the Inter-Society Color Council's 1955 census files it, in block 26, as a light yellowish pink [1]. The Ngram record shows the English phrase peaking in print in 1929, after a slow climb that began around 1879 [3].

In Japan, the same shade is called *sakura-iro* (桜色), cherry blossom color[1]. Its closest library neighbor is [[flesh-pink]], under 3 units away, with [[pale-flesh-color]] close behind; ColorHub's broader map also puts it near [[baby-pink]], a shade lighter still, and [[safrano-pink]] [1]. A fifth, slightly farther neighbor is [[pale-congo-pink]], 5.6 ΔE away, duller [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this pink in just 7 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, always as a highlight [2]. Danish and French paintings carry it a little above the archive's base rate, though the sample is small [2]. The scarcity fits a bright, saturated pink: few aged, varnished canvases hold enough of a color this light and clean across 5 percent of their surface [2]. The count is a computed color match, never a pigment identification [2].
